newsitem.title: USA: Census Bureau oilmill stats said supportive to soy.
newsitem.headline: Census Bureau oilmill stats said supportive to soy.

text.p: The Census Bureau oilmill report released early Thursday based on April activity was mildly supportive to CBOT soybean futures, traders said.
"The crush was pretty good but it all looked pretty neutral to me, maybe a little supportive for beans," a trader said.

The Census Bureau said U.S. soybean crushings during April totaled 114.757 million bushels. That was above an average of analysts' expectations for 113.125 million bushels and above the range of estimates for 112 million to 114 million bushels.
The soyoil and soymeal stocks data was neutral to futures.
Census April soymeal stocks totaled 280,058 tons, above an average of analysts' expectations for 261,500 tons but within the range of estimates from 198,000 to 318,000 tons.
April soyoil stocks totaled 2.164 billion lbs, above the average of analysts' estimates for 2.052 billion lbs and near the high end of expectations for 1.760 billion to 2.166 billion lbs.
Traders early Thursday were expecting CBOT soybean futures to open three to five cents per bushel higher, soymeal $1.00 to $2.00 per ton higher and soyoil 0.10 to 0.20 cent per lb higher.
The calls for a higher opening were based on bullish input from USDA's weekly export sales report with the Census Bureau's report viewed as neutral to supportive, traders said.
